extracted.intended_audience: customs brokers, brokerage firms, accrediting bodies, continuing-education providers, and CBP officials/staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory final-rule economic and implementation guidance describing requirements, acceptable trainings, accreditation, recordkeeping, cost assumptions, benefit estimates, and alternatives for a continuing broker education program requiring 36 hours every three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing broker education requirement (36 hours/3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers are required to complete 36 hours of continuing broker education over a three-year (triennial) period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brokers will be required to spend 36 hours over three years completing continuing broker education in whatever form they choose. CBP models compliance on a triennial cycle; some brokers already meet this and will not face new training-hours requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable forms of qualifying trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying continuing broker education includes webinars, seminars, trade conferences, internal trainings, and other events; free webinars and government-sponsored trainings may qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing broker education that qualifies under the terms of the rule includes webinars, seminars, and trade conferences. Free webinars and trainings hosted by Federal government agencies and identified by CBP will qualify and do not require approval by a CBP-selected accreditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-guided online course standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-guided, online courses or content are acceptable only if they culminate in a retention test and are accredited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP clarifies that self-guided, online courses or content, whether free or paid, which culminate in a retention test are also acceptable if accredited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training accreditation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Coursework/events must be accredited by entities designated by CBP (CBP-selected accreditors) for the training to count under the rule (except certain CBP-identified government trainings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will designate entities or companies as approved accreditors via an RFP process; providers must submit applications to accreditors to have their coursework or events accredited. Free trainings identified by CBP do not require accreditor approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor designation and renewal process
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will solicit applications via RFP to designate accreditors; designation will occur prior to implementation; accreditors must reapply/renew every three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A panel of CBP experts will evaluate applications and select accreditors. The designation process will occur before the continuing broker education requirements go into effect. Accreditors and CBP will need to complete the process three times in a seven-year period (i.e., reapplication every three years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider application and accreditation renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers (course/event sponsors) will need to submit applications to accreditors to obtain accreditation and may need to renew accreditation (annual renewal assumed by CBP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP estimates about 2,000 courses will require accreditation each year; providers will likely pay an accreditation fee (CBP estimates an average fee of $25) and will need to renew their accreditation annually to ensure coursework remains up to date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements for individual brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Brokers must maintain paper or digital copies of documentation received from the provider and a document listing date, title, provider, number of credit hours, and location (if applicable) for each training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brokers must maintain records of their completed continuing broker education and report compliance to CBP. CBP will only require brokers to maintain their records for the three years following the submission of the triennial status report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial reporting mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Brokers report and certify compliance via the triennial status report; paper filers include a written statement, electronic filers use an eCBP checkbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To report and certify compliance, individual brokers who file paper-based triennial status reports with CBP will include a written statement; those who file electronically through eCBP will check a box while filing their triennial status report electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record production upon CBP request
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP may request brokers to produce their continuing education records; brokers must produce records if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will occasionally conduct record requests by randomly selecting a subset of brokers to produce records. CBP estimates producing records (for those selected) will take 15 minutes (0.25 hours) per request.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBP sampling rate for record requests
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP assumes it will request records from 10 percent of active individual brokers per year (covering the most recently completed triennial period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the purposes of this analysis, CBP assumes over the next three years it will request records from 10 percent of active individual brokers each year. CBP estimates about 1,603 record requests performed per year in applicable years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broker time-burden estimates: research, registration, recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP assumes brokers will spend ~3 hours per triennial period researching and registering for trainings, and 0.5 hours per year on recordkeeping; total compliance time ~40.5 hours per three-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP assumes an individual broker will spend approximately three hours finding and registering for continuing broker education during every triennial period. CBP estimates recordkeeping and reporting will take each individual broker 30 minutes (0.5 hours) per year. Overall, brokers will need to spend about 40.5 hours over a three-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broker record-production time for audit/sample
rubrics_metrics.description: When selected for record requests, CBP estimates producing records will take 15 minutes (0.25 hours); CBP expects 10% of brokers will incur this each year after first triennial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the first triennial reporting period in which brokers self-attest, 10 percent of individual brokers each year will incur the cost of producing records to submit to CBP following a record request, which CBP estimates will take 15 minutes (0.25 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-hour training fee assumptions (low/medium/high)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP assumes average hourly monetary cost of qualifying trainings: $0 (low), $30 (medium), $50 (high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption is based on current fees for continuing education certifications, webinars, and trade conferences; CBP notes hourly costs (excluding free events) usually range from around $25 to $70 and fees are often tiered by membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and incidental cost assumptions for in-person events
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP estimates per-conference travel/incidental costs: airfare $332, lodging $288, meals & incidentals $177 (total $797 per conference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP assumes medium-cost brokers travel to one major conference per year (3-day) and high-cost brokers travel to two per year. Over a triennial (36-hour) period, travel adds $66 per credit hour (medium) or $133 per credit hour (high).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-credit hour total cost calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP calculates per-credit hour cost as: hourly training fee + research/registration cost per credit ($2.90) + travel per-credit-hour. Resulting per-credit-hour totals: $2.90 (low), $99 (medium), $186 (high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and registration cost is assumed constant at $2.90 per credit hour (based on 3 hours per triennial and loaded wage). Travel per-credit-hour is computed by spreading multi-year travel costs across 36 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost valuation method
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP uses an average loaded wage rate of $34.81 per hour to value brokers' time (opportunity cost) for training, research, and recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the loaded wage rate, CBP estimates opportunity costs of researching, registering for, attending, and reporting continuing broker education to compute aggregate and per-broker opportunity costs over the analysis period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary estimate assumption for brokers' cost-path selection
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP's primary estimate assumes one third of individual brokers will elect each cost path (low, medium, high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP uses the equal-split assumption because it cannot predict which option each broker will choose; this drives the 'primary' cost estimate vs. all-low or all-high scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider volume and fee estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP estimates ~2,000 courses will require accreditation each year and assumes an average accreditation fee of $25 per course (yielding $350,000 in provider costs over seven years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate based on NCBFAA Education Institute's current approvals (~1,000/year) and expected increase when rule requires accreditation of internal trainings and external offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor application cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP estimates application/preparation to become an accreditor will take two employees 40 hours each, per application cycle; accreditors will apply three times over seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP estimates CBP-selected accreditors will incur approximately $17,182 in costs over the seven-year analysis period for preparing applications (tabled per-cycle wage assumptions used).

rubrics_metrics.name: CBP personnel costs to designate accreditors
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP estimates designation requires six CBP personnel 180 hours total per designation cycle, three cycles in seven years, cost $59,260.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP models time to develop/submit RFP (2 personnel, 10 hours each) and application evaluation (4 personnel, 40 hours each) and spreads costs across three designation cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBP record-request processing cost per request
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP estimates each continuing broker education record request will take approximately one hour and cost CBP approximately $109.74 per request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP assumes 1,603 record requests per year in applicable years, resulting in $527,603 in record-request costs over the seven-year analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit metric — audits avoided
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP projects continuing education will avoid approximately 40 percent of audits; average audit is 593 hours and costs CBP $65,049 each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP projects avoiding 33 audits over seven years (savings of $2,133,623) based on historical audit rates (average 14 per year) and the estimated reduction due to continuing education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit metric — penalties reduced
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP projects individual brokers will commit approximately 20 percent fewer penalizable violations under the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 2017-2021, average monetary penalties collected from individual brokers were $2,423; CBP estimates fines avoided and CBP processing costs avoided using per-penalty cost ($6,584) and projected baseline penalty counts (99 per year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evidence of effectiveness (statistical finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP's analysis found, at the 99 percent confidence level, that companies employing brokers who voluntarily hold a continuing-education-linked certification have significantly lower rates of penalties, audits, and validation activities (ratios: 13:1 penalties, 7:1 audits, 9:1 validation activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This comparison is based on a group of about 120 companies (representing ~53-54% of entries filed) versus the broader population; CBP uses this as supporting evidence for expected benefits from mandatory continuing education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Brokers must retain continuing education records for three years following the submission of the triennial status report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will only require individual brokers to maintain their records for this three-year period, after which retention is not required by the rule as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives considered and rejection rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP considered Alternative 1 (72 hours every three years) and Alternative 3 (CBP-public list of brokers voluntarily meeting standards); CBP selected 36 hours as the chosen approach and rejected 72 hours as too onerous, especially for small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP modeled costs for 72 hours and estimated substantially higher aggregate costs (up to $284,775,217 over seven years). CBP judged 72 hours would require many brokers to increase training by ~100% and be especially burdensome for small firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCBP reporting update (implementation note)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will add a field within the electronic triennial status report (eCBP) to allow brokers to self-attest to continuing education completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP notes the programming to include this field is minor and does not significantly increase application development budgets, as CBP routinely makes small changes to electronic data interchanges.
